loc.1.0:
You successfully repelled the soldiers' attack on the heart of the pirate base, but the matter doesn't end here. Now you must work your way through tunnels already crawling with soldiers to reach the entrance of the military base itself. 
The mission isn't easy, but you don't have a choice.
Fortunately, you tore to shreds all of the foes attacking the pirate base, so you have a couple of minutes for a peaceful pastime unrelated to rabid shooting, deafening explosions, and gushing blood.
loc.2.0: You moved forward, mostly because in the tunnel you didn't have a lot of other ways to go, except backward. The tunnel curved slightly to the right, so you couldn't see what was happening ahead. Happily, by listening carefully you were soon able to determine that a large number of soldiers was marching ahead. You moved forward a little more, pressing against the wall, until you saw that your tunnel intersected with another tunnel along which a massive crowd of armored mercenaries with weapons in their hands was advancing.
loc.2.1: You rested against the wall and waited, occasionally yawning into your fist. Unfortunately, after one detachment had passed and you were about to step forward, another detachment appeared from the tunnel, with another close behind. Because your plans don't include dying there from old age, you probably need to go somewhere else. What's more, it is entirely possible that the next detachment will turn in your direction.
loc.4.0:
You look left and right and noticed a ventilation hole in the wall, not far from you. The bolts holding in the grate were rusted through, so it didn't cramp your style to break into the ventilation shaft.
Once inside you immediately raised a cloud of old dust and held in a sneeze by sheer willpower alone. After determining the direction in which you were moving, you crawled along the shaft. You soon discovered that you were not alone here. Some little stinker, which you identified as a space rodent (a nyru), bit you painfully on the finger. Apparently, nobody had done any utility work or cleaning at this pirate base in a long time, because you soon observed a whole colony of nyrus on the move. A couple of them also decided to see what you taste like, so you had to defend yourself. Fortunately, the shaft ended soon with another ventilation hole and the grate covering it literally crumbled to pieces in your hands. You freed yourself and discovered that you were in a small hangar. 
Looking around, you spotted small gates with the word "Warehouse" written on them, and next to the gates, a transporter on a gravitational pad. Examining the writing on the side more carefully, you realized that this was a faeyan T-3400 transporter. To your right, a glass booth is illuminated from within. The dirty glass makes it impossible to determine whether or not someone is inside. Along the very center of the hangar, on the wall opposite from you, are the large gates of the airlock.
loc.4.1:
You are in the center of the hangar. 
At your left are small gates with the word "Warehouse" written on them, and next to the gates, there is a transporter on a gravitational pad. From the writing on the side, it follows that this is a faeyan T-3400 transporter. To your right, a glass booth is illuminated from within. The dirty glass makes it impossible to determine whether or not someone is inside. Along the very center of the hangar, on the wall opposite from you, are the large gates of the airlock.
loc.4.2:
The gates were clearly designed for the T-3400 transporter in the hangar. You examined the gates closely but could not find a control panel to open them. They must work some other way.
You sighed in disappointment and returned to your original position.
loc.5.0: Waiting turned out to be a disaster for you. The next military detachment turned into your tunnel and began to draw unavoidably closer. You unglued yourself from the wall and began to retreat, but not quickly enough, and the mercenaries noticed you. Shouts of commands could be heard along the tunnel, and in an instant a hailstorm of fire from weapons of various calibers descended upon you. The bullets and charges ricocheted off the walls, exacerbating the situation. You hit the floor and crawled, but then a stray bullet struck you in the back, paralyzing you. Then it was easy for the mercenaries to catch you and finish you off with a couple of shots at point-blank.
loc.6.0: The silvery T-3400 transporter on the gravitational pad was parked by the gates to the warehouse, which were hospitably thrown open. However, this most likely means that there's nothing left inside.
loc.6.1: You tugged on transporter's side hatch, but it wouldn't budge. It's as if you need a key to get into the T-3400.
loc.6.2: The silvery T-3400 transporter on the gravitational pad was parked by the gates to the warehouse.
loc.7.0: The gates are evidently made for T-3400 transporter, which also was in the hangar. You've checked them carefully, but couldn't find control panel to open them. Probably, they work some other way.
loc.9.0: You carefully stole up to the booth and peeked into the slightly open door. There was a maloq in a mercenary uniform, probably left here to guard the transporter. Judging by his desperate yawning and sleepy eyes, life hasn't been too interesting for him lately.
loc.9.1: The maloq you cut down is lying in the glass booth. Man, it would be really strange if he weren't.
loc.10.0:
You are inside the warehouse, which is barely illuminated by a couple of lights. All the racks and shelves are empty. All kinds of junk, torn packaging, and some small broken parts are strewn all over the floor,
A note was fixed to the other side of the gates: "The warehouse has been relocated. The new location is Depot 13."
loc.10.1: You diligently picked through the junk pile paving the floor and good fortune unexpectedly smiled upon you - you found a bunch of smoke grenades which were dropped while the supplies were being moved.
loc.12.0:
You gathered your courage, let out a yell, and burst into the booth, nearly catching your foot on the raised threshold. Fortunately, the maloq was so taken aback by your appearance that he recoiled and toppled from the chair. You threw yourself on top of him, pinning him to the ground and pummeling him with your fists. Unfortunately, your opponent quickly pulled himself together and gave you a couple of good blows to the torso. This infuriated you and you brought the chair down on top of him repeatedly until he stopped quivering.
Catching your breath after the skirmish, you checked the mercenary's pockets and found a key with a tag labeled "T-3400". When you were finished with his pockets, you also took his blaster. Looking inside, you observed that a monitor was built into the panel the maloq was sitting next to, and presently it was showing the layout of the base's nearby tunnels. Just in case, you studied the information and tried to memorize it.
loc.12.1:
You tore out the pin of a grenade with your teeth, for toughness, and then lobbed it into the booth. There was a blast, and puffs of choking smoke drifted through the slightly open door. The maloq, judging by the crashing sound, toppled off his chair in surprise and dashed for the exit. All you have left to do is go in at the entrance and whack him on the head. After being hit, the maloq submissively buried his nose in the floor and lost consciousness.
You checked the mercenary's pockets and found a key with a tag labeled "T-3400" in one of them. When you were finished with his pockets, you also took his blaster.
Then you threw open the door wider and entered the booth after first throwing a smoke bomb in. Looking inside, you observed that a monitor was built into the panel the maloq was sitting next to, and presently it was showing the layout of the base's nearby tunnels. Just in case, you studied the information and tried to memorize it.
loc.13.0:
The key you took from the maloq proved indeed to belong to the transporter. You came five steps closer, the T-3400 chirped a greeting and the side hatch unlocked with a click. You climbed inside the transporter and looked around. The controls appeared to be entirely old school, so you ought not have any problems with them. You also searched for a button to activate the onboard weaponry, but could not find one - meaning that the T-3400 has no weaponry. You plunged into depression, but you were distracted by the control unit for the Jumpmeter - a special device that allows the transporter to jump into the air given a sufficient charge level.
Brightening up, you started the transporter and drove up to the gates, hoping that this would help you figure out how to open them. This helped indeed, because a light built into the transporter began flashing and the gates lifted by themselves. The path was clear.

You followed the straight tunnel, which sloped downward slightly, because there was no place to turn around. After about five hundred meters you came to a crossroads where some joker had placed an enormous planter and driven in a stake with signs, which gave you to understand that the path to the left leads to the "Distillation Room", while the path to the right leads to the "Sorting Room", and the path straight ahead gets you to "Depot 13".

While you reflected on where you should go first, a small red light began blinking on the control panel, indicating that the fuel level was low. You flicked the gauge with your fingernail. Alas, this didn't raise the fuel level! Apparently, the first order of business is to find a fuel station.
loc.13.1: You are at a dimly lit intersection. The signs on the walls say that you can head toward the "Distillation Room", the "Sorting Room", or "Depot 13".
loc.13.2:
Small and speedy nyrus with sharp teeth are the real scourge of every old space station. You tested this proposition on yourself while on foot along the tunnel. Consequently, the walk wasn't very pleasant.
You are now at a dimly lit intersection. The signs on the walls say that you can head toward the "Distillation Room", the "Sorting Room", or "Depot 13".
loc.14.0:
You passed through the gates, which closed again behind your back, and found yourself on a narrow platform about twenty meters long. Immediately beyond the platform is an abrupt precipice, and the next platform is at a lower level and located some distance from the one you are on.
Reviewing the big picture, you determined that to move between platforms a special freight elevator is used, controlled from a booth located on the lower platform. You looked closer and observed some sort of peleng in the booth, who has not yet noticed you.

You can't use the Jumpmeter either, because a low ceiling hangs above the platform and if you jumped, you would risk making a hole in the ceiling. Or perhaps a hole in the transporter. In either case, your T-3400 would be unlikely to run afterward.
loc.14.1: Even over the noise of the transporter's running motor you can hear the roar of the peleng's stereovision showing a hatchball match. He probably couldn't hear you even if you wanted him to.
loc.14.2: You squeezed the trigger of your machine gun for a moment, firing a short burst toward the booth, but you missed and the peleng didn't even notice what happened.
loc.16.0: Passing the wide airlock gates, you found yourself in Depot 13, an enormous warehouse, the far side of which was barely visible somewhere in the distance. Perhaps something amongst the equipment here could be adapted to your transporter.
loc.16.1:
Passing the wide airlock gates, you found yourself in Depot 13, an enormous warehouse, the far side of which was barely visible somewhere in the distance. Perhaps something amongst the equipment here could be adapted to your transporter.
The light on the control panel began to blink treacherously. Apparently, the fuel was gone and something had to be done quickly.
loc.16.2: Passing the wide airlock gates, you found yourself in Depot 13, an enormous warehouse, the far side of which was barely visible somewhere in the distance. Perhaps something amongst the equipment here could be adapted to your transporter.
loc.16.3: Passing the wide airlock gates, you found yourself in Depot 13, an enormous warehouse, the far side of which was barely visible somewhere in the distance. Perhaps something amongst the equipment here could be adapted to your transporter, which is still waiting for your return.
loc.16.4: You donned your thinking cap and realized that first of all you need to get hold of some fuel, because the transporter won't go without it. So you climbed out, grabbed a fuel can from the cargo compartment, and set off to find somebody who would give you some flammable liquid.
loc.16.5: In the body, you found a funnel, stuck it into the fuel hole, and poured fuel from the can. Now you have something to run on, but not for very long. After all, the fuel tank is big and the transporter eats as much fuel as anyone could want. Refueling clearly won't bother you.
loc.16.6: You loaded your T-3400 with enough sweet gizmos and cool frills to make yourself feel noticeably more confident.
loc.18.0: You are inside Depot 13. You are surrounded on all sides by enormous racks crammed with everything you could want and a little bit of junk. Perhaps something here could even be adapted to your transporter. The important thing is to remember that its payload capacity is only <clr>120<clrEnd> bug. Anything more and it physically will not fly.
loc.18.1: The equipment is great, but don't forget that there is much else that is interesting on the other racks.
loc.18.2: You believed that the weaponry you've already taken will be sufficient to transform your peaceful T-3400 transporter into a machine capable of inflicting death and destruction on your enemies. Now you just need to get busy installing it. You grabbed the last parts and walked away from the racks holding a weapon.
loc.18.3: You decided to also look after yourself, just in case you and your transporter suddenly ended up taking off in different directions. After rummaging through the shelves, you found a little ammunition and were also lucky enough to find a motherboard compatible with your blaster, which will now be able to shoot bursts of rounds.
loc.19.0:
After a lengthy examination of the numerous racks, you determined that you need the following equipment:

- Powerful light/spotlight
- Military radar
- Electromagnetic field suppressor
- Turbocharger for the engine
- Navigator

You found only one of each item, but don't worry. They're still so heavy that there wouldn't be any point to taking more than one of each onboard.
loc.19.1:
You snatched a light from the shelf and dragged it toward the transporter, huffing and puffing. 
Good choice. Now you won't be afraid of the base's dark corridors.
loc.19.2: There is no question that the radar will be useful - it can help you detect things that you cannot see with your own eyes. If it weren't so heavy, it would be priceless.
loc.19.3: You took the electromagnetic suppressor more because of its awesome name than rational thought, because it isn't likely to come in handy. But on other hand, now you can proudly boast that your T-3400 is equipped with this sophisticated device.
loc.19.4: You thought it over and came to the conclusion that in your situation it would be better to take truly useful items. After all, the success of your mission and indeed your life, depend on their presence or absence. So you removed the electromagnetic suppressor and left it lying on the floor next to the transporter.
loc.19.5: The value of the navigator is undeniable, indeed with it you'll never get lost no matter where you go. So grabbing that device wasn't in vain.
loc.19.6: Panting and exclaiming a few bad words, you installed the turbocharger on the transporter's engine, while getting covered with motor oil up to your ears. But now you're less likely to be late to your appointments - and breaking away from your pursuers will be much easier.
loc.19.7: You carried plates of armor to the transporter and then wasted no time putting them where they go. And so what if the T-3400 is noticeably heavier? Now it looks super cool - and you don't have to be afraid of a shoot-out. Now you don't even have to violate your conscience to call it an armored transporter.
loc.20.0: Oh, yes. This here is definitely something to get your hands on. Your eyes even began to move independently a bit, but you immediately brought them back into place by the force of your will.
loc.20.1: You picked up the machine gun and emitted a sinister laugh. Now the soldiers and mercenaries that may encounter you along the way will have to pay - you just need to get within firing range.
loc.20.2: You recalled several times in your life when, at the most inopportune moment, you ran out of ammunition and wisely decided to take another box. You lifted it from the rack and, wobbling, dragged it to the transporter, and then threw it into the cargo compartment.
loc.20.3: A sniper's weapon is a considerable advantage in any skirmish at a distance. The important thing is to make your adjustments when firing in order to accurately hit the target. That's why snipers' victims always feel a little cheated, though they can no longer complain about this.
loc.20.4: No doubt about it, a grenade launcher is heavy, shoots slowly, and doesn't have many extra rounds. But when it fires, you find all of this easy to forgive. In a desperate moment there's nothing better than having a grenade launcher on hand. So you spared no effort and carried the grenade launcher to the transporter.
loc.20.9: You resolved to lighten your means of transportation and abandon whatever you felt was unnecessary.
loc.25.0:
You decided to try to rapidly accelerate and jump to the lower platform. To do that you would need to squeeze every last bit of power out of the transporter's engine.
After returning to the gates, you swung around, smashed the accelerator to the floor, and the transporter shot forward with the engine growling furiously. I believed that everything had already worked out, but a couple of meters before the end of the platform the engine choked on some fuel and suddenly cut out. The transporter lost its speed, but you had no hope of stopping it at this point. The transporter tipped over the edge of the platform and flew downward - and after twenty seconds or so smashed into smithereens against the ground.
loc.26.0:
You decided to try to rapidly accelerate and jump to the lower platform. To do that you would need to squeeze every last bit of power out of the transporter's engine.
After returning to the gates, you swung around, smashed the accelerator to the floor, and the transporter shot forward with the engine growling furiously. The jump was a complete success. Not only did you leap across to the lower platform, you flew all the way to the booth with the peleng, easily crushing it with the front part of the transporter. Peeking out, you observed that the hatchball fan had flown headlong into the stereovision screen, instantly finishing him off. Well, that's one less problem to deal with.

You moved in reverse, banging and clattering the pieces of the booth, until the transporter was entirely free, then turned and drove to the middle of the platform. After driving forward a little, you saw that farther ahead the entire platform was covered on one side with damaged transporters, mostly older models. They didn't stop you from driving by on the cleared side of the platform. 
After traveling about a kilometer, you came upon an intersection which, like the last one, had been furnished with a huge pot with plants and signs. Remembering the map you saw at the location where you expropriated the transporter, you understood that the path to the right would lead to guard post, while the path to the left would lead to the Movable Corridors. Heading to the guard wouldn't be worth it - that's the main tunnel, which is probably heavily protected by the army's forces, and if you were to turn up there it would seriously shorten your lifespan.

loc.29.0: You traveled a couple hundred meters in peace and quiet then came across another departure in which several supply columns, including transporters, were moving. You decided to take advantage of this, because you needed to cross several hundred meters to reach the other side in order to turn into the next side tunnel.
loc.29.1: You hit the gas and tried to squeeze between a few transporters, but you managed to see in time that you wouldn't be able to elbow your way in due to a lack of speed. You need to do something quickly before the other drivers take an interest in your strange driving.
loc.30.0:
You waited for a break in the columns and then boisterously fell in behind one of them. You transporter differed little from the others, because you calmly rode behind the rest of the transporters, unnoticed by anyone.
When the corridor you were hoping to reach was just a few tens of meters away, the entire column suddenly came to a halt. There seemed to be a small traffic jam. Talking filled the air, then you realized with horror that the station where the column had stopped had begun a roll call. You need to take some action before your presence is detected.
loc.30.1:
You activated a laser and a thin beam pierced the transporter standing in front of you. Unfortunately, the beam's intensity wasn't sufficient to burn through the metal hull - you only succeeded in damaging the paint. Neither did the next shot produce the desired effect. 
You need to think of something else that's more effective.
loc.32.0:
After skillfully spinning the steering wheel, you forced yourself between two gravicars and joined the general traffic. Your maneuver was accompanied by brief cursing over the radio, but apparently nobody suspected a thing. The turbocharger upgrade to the engine was most welcome. Just a few minutes later you reached the side exit you were hoping for and immediately turned into it with gusto. If someone chewed you out for this maneuver, you didn't hear it.

Traveling several meters down the narrow tunnel, you entered an average-sized hall which was obviously designed for storing some sort of hazardous waste. You determined this by the fact that the entire hall was crammed with large barrels with warning labels - and the disgusting odor that pushed its way through even the air filter of your T-3400. Gates could be seen on the far side of the hall.
loc.32.1:
Rightfully deciding that a bit of panic in this chaos wouldn't bother anything, you fired a short burst from the machine gun at the gravicar parked ahead. Your assessment was correct. Finding himself on fire, the driver instinctively hit the gas and consequently his transporter roared forward and smashed into the transporter in front of him, which due to inertia crashed into the one in front it, and so on down the line. Thus, the entire column lurched forward a bit, freeing the entry to your precious tunnel. You plunged into without giving the members of the column time to think about what had happened and who was to blame.

You laughed sinisterly and let fly a rocket at the transporter in front of you. It immediately burst into flames, and after a few moments it exploded. The rest of the drivers instantly dashed toward the station, breaking formation to protect their transporters from the conflagration. You skillfully drove around the hot debris and turned into the side exit without giving the members of the column time to think about what had happened and who was to blame.

loc.34.0: The gates were closed and showed no response to the approach of your transporter. This is most likely because they are frequently blocked by barrels. You already wanted to ram them, but you were troubled by the odor, which stubbornly confirmed that something flammable was in the barrels and it could go up in a big bang.
loc.34.1: You let out a full burst from the machine gun at one of the barrels, but it honorably withstood your treatment. It must have super durable walls if machine gun rounds only bounce off helplessly.
loc.36.0:
You aimed carefully at the cover of the drain hole on one of the barrels standing near the gates, and fired. A deafening explosion confirmed that you had not missed your target. Burning debris flew in every direction and several more barrels detonated in other parts of the hall.

When everything around stopped exploding, you opened your eyes and noticed that the gates were now clear. What's more, several of the exploding barrels had opened a dark passage that you had not previously noticed, leading somewhere in the same direction as the gates.
loc.36.1:
You aimed the rocket launcher in the direction of one of the barrels standing near the gates, and fired. A deafening explosion confirmed that you had not missed your target. But even if you had missed it wouldn't have changed anything. Burning debris flew in every direction and several more barrels detonated in other parts of the hall.

When everything around stopped exploding, you opened your eyes and noticed that the gates were now clear. What's more, several of the exploding barrels had opened a dark passage that you had not previously noticed, leading somewhere in the same direction as the gates.
loc.36.2:
Suffering from the unbearable stench in the air, you began to pick at the cover of the drain hole on one of the barrels. In the end, after painfully pinching your finger and spilling some of the flammable liquid onto your pants, you succeeded in your task. Then you move to where the fuel was beginning to flow, ignited it, and with all your might dashed to the transporter. You had hardly climbed inside when a deafening explosion sounded. Burning debris flew in every direction and several more barrels detonated in other parts of the hall.

When everything around stopped exploding, you opened your eyes and noticed that the gates were now clear. What's more, several of the exploding barrels had opened a dark passage that you had not previously noticed, leading somewhere in the same direction as the gates.
loc.36.3: You checked the radar, which correctly indicated that somebody was in the hangar behind the gates. Judging by the positions they had taken, these were most likely soldiers who were ready to meet you immediately beyond the gates. You too need to be ready for this.
loc.36.4: You checked the navigator, which confirmed that the dark tunnel was an alternative way to get into the same hangar to which the gates led. If you could pass through this tunnel, your appearance would be a surprise to the potential enemies waiting for you in the hangar.
loc.38.0:
You moved forward, trying to stay away from the potholes in the road so some absurd accident didn't stop your important and high-ranking mission. When the engine suddenly failed, you just shook your head, amazed at your own prophetic insight. If this could happen with an ordinary pothole, who knows what else might happen. Meanwhile, the transporter conked out completely. Even the cabin light died, which you took to be a bad sign. Fortunately, the start button worked properly and the revived engine again began to rumble cheerfully. 
You started to wonder what all that was, but there was no time to sit and think. So you started off again, eyeing the instrument panel suspiciously.

You started to wonder what all that was, but there was no time to sit and think. So you started off again, eyeing the instrument panel suspiciously.
loc.38.2: You had barely traveled a couple of meters when the engine again stuttered and fell silent. You cursed and started checking the instrument readings, beginning with the fuel level. Strangely, everything seemed to be in order. You pressed the start button and the engine began to work again - though not for the first time. Apparently, neither you nor the engine enjoyed these sudden shutdowns. You need to determine what's going on after all. Otherwise, after the next shutdown the engine may stop working altogether.
loc.38.3: You gingerly stuck your head out of the transporter and looked about. You didn't detect anything suspicious. But you could hide a whole platoon between the beams and the ceiling, so you need to stay on guard.
loc.38.4: The radar has identified a fat blob in the direction of your heading, implying that a potential enemy is sitting directly on the nose of your transporter. It's not likely to be a frightened pirate builder - they've all long since fled. Unfortunately, he has taken up a position outside the reach of your weapons, and now you must think up some way to deal with him. A bit farther ahead the radar shows some sort of power unit. You might try doing something with it.
loc.39.0:
You entered the hangar, passing through the open gates, and immediately the transporter was assailed by shots from blasters - not especially dangerous, but unpleasant just the same. You took in the situation and realized that they were shooting at you from two large barricades built from bags of some sort of building material. Near the barricade on the right you noticed several of the barrels that love to explode which you have become acquainted with.
You need to decide what to do now before one of the shots hits some vulnerable spot on your T-3400. You are nearly certain that such vulnerabilities exist.
loc.39.1:
You entered the hangar through the open gates and immediately opened fire in the direction indicated by the radar. Only after beginning to shoot did you look closely and notice that you were shooting up two large barricades built from bags with some sort of building material inside. Fortunately, not all of your shots were stopped by the cover and some of the enemies behind the left barricade no longer showed signs of life. Near the barricade on the right you noticed several of the barrels that love to explode so loudly and colorfully.
While you were looking around, your enemies recovered from your unexpected attack and began fire at your from blasters. They aren't capable of inflicting great harm, but they still aren't very pleasant.
You need to decide what to do now before one of the shots hits some vulnerable spot on your T-3400. You are nearly certain that such vulnerabilities exist.
loc.39.2:
You entered the hangar through the open gates, but first lobbed in a grenade as a preventative measure. It cost you to enter the hangar all the way, because immediately the transporter was assailed by shots from blasters - not especially dangerous, but unpleasant just the same. You took in the situation and realized that they were shooting at you from two large barricades built from bags of some sort of building material. Near the barricade on the right you noticed several of the barrels that love to explode, while the left barricade was partially destroyed by your grenade, some of the attackers behind it no longer showing signs of life.
You need to decide what to do now before one of the shots hits some vulnerable spot on your T-3400. You are nearly certain that such vulnerabilities exist.
loc.39.3: The blaster charges are striking the sheathing of your transporter, leaving scorch marks. Apparently, your enemies did not intend to surrender. Rather they burned with a desire to annihilate the hated T-3400 and you together with it.
loc.39.4: At some point you became outraged at the injustice of the fact that there were many enemies attacking you, but there was only one you. You even wanted to climb out of the transporter and scream at them that they weren't fighting fair and that they should come face you one at a time. But then it occurred to you that then you would have to climb out of your T-3400 - and that was the last thing you wanted to do. And nobody would be likely to hear you in the heat of battle.  Instead, your enemies would be thrilled that you personally showed yourself in their blasters' sights.
loc.39.5: Sparks and explosions entirely surround you. Warning messages blink on the transporter's displays. The flashes of gunfire are thrown about the hangar. Ah, an honest-to-goodness war. It leaves you breathless. The important thing now is to stay sharp and not waste munitions.
loc.39.6: You carefully took aim, ignoring your foe's gunfire, and took a shot. The barrel obediently exploded, shattering into burning fragments, some of which flew toward the bags of the right barricade. Several enemies, on fire, leapt out from behind the barricade, filling the air with their screams. Looks like you pulled off a totally lucky shot.
loc.41.0:
You returned fire and returned fire until, finally, you noticed that the enemy was no longer shooting back. You squinted your eyes slyly and peered through the observational screens, suspecting a trap - but there wasn't one. It turns out you really did shoot everyone down. No one will continue to hinder your progress, so you can move on.
Leaving the hangar through the gates opposite those through which you entered, you laid on the gas pedal and carried on quick as the wind. Less than ten minutes later, you saw an orange and red barrier, signaling the fact that repairs are underway up ahead. You looked closely and saw that the path had been dismantled in places; in some places the beams and covering remained intact, but where they were missing, dark chasms, which ought not to be fallen into, gaped wide. The upper portion of the tunnel was also dismantled, but the coverings were narrower there.
loc.41.1: Without incident you rolled along the dimly lit tunnel and came to the conclusion that the entire pirate base has extremely poor lighting. Nevertheless, this did not prevent you from pushing forward to fulfill your mission. Suddenly, you saw an orange and red barrier up ahead, signaling the fact that somebody decided to make repairs at the place where you had only just arrived. You looked closely and saw that the path had been dismantled in places; in some places the beams and covering remained intact, but where they were missing, dark chasms, which ought not to be fallen into, gaped wide. The upper portion of the tunnel was also dismantled, but the coverings were narrower there.
loc.41.2:
You entered the hangar in a place entirely unexpected by the soldiers. You understood this when you observed them twenty meters off, standing with their backs to you and staring intently in the direction of the gates. They were hiding behind two barricades made of bags. Even more gladdening to your heart was the sight of the portable heavy weapon that these guys left in the rear, clearly not planning to use it against you. Unfortunately for them, you decided to use it, and after two bursts - one for each of the barricades - the ambush was over. Like they say, they didn't even know what hit them.
Leaving the hangar through the gates opposite those through which you entered, you laid on the gas pedal and carried on quick as the wind. Less than ten minutes later, you saw an orange and red barrier, signaling the fact that repairs are underway up ahead. You looked closely and saw that the path had been dismantled in places; in some places the beams and covering remained intact, but where they were missing, dark chasms, which ought not to be fallen into, gaped wide. The upper portion of the tunnel was also dismantled, but the coverings were narrower there.
loc.43.0:
The idea crept into your head that somebody up ahead was playing around with an electromagnetic transmitter. You decided to deliver a response. 
"Hey, scumbags! You're still gonna pay for San Holo!" you screamed angrily and pressed the suppressor's activation button.
It's not clear what happened after that, because visually nothing changed around your transporter. But the engine stopped cutting out, so unimpeded you drove onward and quickly surmounted the dangerous section of the path.
loc.43.1:
You sent off your final shot at the target with precision and took no small satisfaction in seeing that your vanquished foe together with his blaster had tumbled out of the booth and fallen cleanly below into one of the gaps between the beams. Even if he had still been alive, the fall would probably have finished him off.
Returning to the transporter, you easily started the engine, which no longer cut out, and drove onward. You reached the end of the dangerous section without incident.
loc.44.0:
You climbed out of the transporter to do some reconnaissance, but you didn't have to languish in obscurity for very long. You hadn't even covered ten meters when blaster shots began flying at you from somewhere above. One of the rounds barely brushed your hand, but it still hurt a lot. You threw yourself behind a segment of plating that was jutting out vertically, which was an incredible stroke of luck for you, and it saved you from the next round which proved to be better aimed. Fortunately, the plating was too thick for the blaster's charge to penetrate.
You cautiously peeked out from behind your cover and immediately pulled back, but you managed to see that up ahead a glass enclosure was lashed to the beams - and the barrel of a blaster was protruding from it. You didn't get a good look at who was holding it.
In theory, you could shoot in the direction of the enclosure without aiming. Maybe you'll hit something. Or it may be better to first find a more convenient shooting position. Your choice.
loc.44.1:
You darted out from your cover and sped toward the enclosure, dodging and evading the shots, a couple of which nearly put some extra holes in you, while a couple others grazed you. Finally, feeling that you were just a moment away from being shot down, you leapt into a narrow gap between two beams.
Your gamble was justified. Now you could see the scoundrel who was firing at you from the enclosure on the ceiling - some dude in working clothes with a blaster in his hands. What upset you most was his personal force field generator. You determined this by the slight warping of the air around him.
You are clearly not on equal ground, but you've got to do something. You can't hide between the beams for the rest of your life.
loc.44.2: You leapt out from behind your cover and ran several meters toward your enemy's position. By the time he got oriented and opened fire, you had again hidden behind one of the beams. Cautiously peeking out from your shelter, you saw not only your enemy's blaster, but also part of the top of his head - meaning your chances of a hit increased slightly.
loc.44.3: It became very uncomfortable for you behind this cover being raked with fire, which was barely protecting you from your opponent's shots. You threw yourself forward in order to find something more reliable. After running a couple of meters and nearly tripping on a cable sticking up out of the floor, you threw yourself behind one of the thick vertical beams before a blaster round could punch an unnecessary hole in you.
loc.44.4: You carefully took aim and squeezed the trigger of your blaster, paying no attention to the shots fired in return, one of which pierced your hand. Fortunately, at that moment you had already shot and hit your mark, judging by the loud cursing emanating from the enclosure under the ceiling.
loc.44.5: You put your hand out from behind the cover and began showering the enclosure under the ceiling with unaimed bursts, holding back nothing. It's not clear if you landed any shots, but you definitely got hit again. It was extremely painful.
loc.44.6: You carefully took aim at the power unit suspended beneath the ceiling behind your enemy's enclosure and shot it a couple of times. One of the shots was a dead hit. The unit exploded, nearly blinding you with an intense flash, and a wave of electricity burst outward in every direction. When it reached the enclosure in an instant, there was a cry of pain and a shower of sparks. As you were expecting, the enemy's force field experienced an extreme overload and went kaput. Now you have every chance of ending the fight on your terms.
loc.47.0:
You passed several lateral tunnels which your transporter simply wouldn't fit in and almost ran into a guard post where you noticed a couple of large-caliber cannons. It wouldn't help to poke your head in there. So you quickly turned into an inconspicuous offshoot from the main tunnel and found yourself at the entrance to a car wash. But this was not an ordinary wash, but rather a full-fledged cleaning workshop, capable of stripping both dirt and paint from filthy vehicles. 
Moving back a bit, you studied the situation but couldn't find an alternative path. The only thing for you to do is put the transporter on the moving conveyor belt and go through the wash. But after being cleaned your T-3400 will glow like a polished skeleton. You didn't like this analogy, but that's too bad. You have to keep moving forward.

You examined the warning signs at the entrance and discovered that the cleaning process uses harmful chemicals that can cause suffocation and death, and therefore drivers must exit their vehicles and go into the pedestrian tunnel built off to the side. Unfortunately, its entrance was blocked by a metal plate which would likely not even be appropriately affected by the weapons on your transporter. So you have to ride in the transporter. Oh well, you're no stranger to risking your life. After all, you're a ranger.
loc.47.1:
Near the entrance, you found a chart showing how the car wash operates. It showed that the conveyer belt moves at <clr>1<clrEnd> m per second. Automatic jets that spray chemicals are located at [p53], [p54], [p55], [p56], and [p57] meters and are activated for <clr>2<clrEnd> seconds every <clr>3<clrEnd> seconds. It is vitally important that you are not in the spray zone, not only while the sprayers are emitting chemicals, but also immediately before they are turned on.

And you can't quickly fly across the whole conveyer belt, because it is equipped with blocking gates that open on the computer's command only as a stationary object approaches. If you drive forward, you risk crashing into the gates, which won't open in time.
loc.48.0:
At first you proceeded very carefully, but then accelerated beyond your driving abilities and flew into a cloud of chemicals. You instantly held your breath and shut your eyes tightly, but nothing bad happened. You opened your eyes and observed that you are still alive. 
How great was your astonishment when you noticed that the armor you had installed on the transporter absorbed every last drop of the toxic spray. What kind of material is this anyway? Satisfied that everything was okay, you calmly reached the end of the conveyer belt without paying any mind to the chemicals. When you exited the car wash the armor simply crumbled off the hull from the slightest bump. Apparently, the chemicals burned it like fire burns wood. Well, it saved you from death. It would be hard to ask for more. But it's time for you to move on.
loc.48.1: Finally, the conveyer belt ended and you stopped in front of the exit gates. Wiping the sweat from your face, you sucked in a deep breath and drove away from the car wash. You came extremely close to the chemical spray a couple of times, which gave you a few new very visible gray hairs. On the other hand, the car wash is behind you and you can move forward.
loc.50.0:
You cautiously drove onto the conveyer belt. The gates of the car wash closed automatically, and as soon as the transporter was completely inside, the conveyer belt began moving. You crept forward and the conveyer belt carried you, slowing reaching its operating speed.
Now the important thing is for you to calculate correctly and avoid being caught under a stream of toxic chemicals.
loc.50.1: You move forward with the conveyer belt, slowly but surely. So far, so good.
loc.53.0: You were going along fine, but fouled things up by flying right into a cloud of chemicals. The transporter's air filters were useless against them and you inhaled the mixture of toxins Breathing became difficult. Red circles floated in front of your eyes and you started to cough. You didn't last another five minutes.
loc.55.0:
You went down the next tunnel for a long time, which began to make you feel nauseous, until you found yourself in the next hall, which served as a storage room for all kinds of junk. At least that's the impression it gave you. Heaps of assorted metallic trash lay in uneven rows, but you dodged between them on your T-3400, following a narrow, crooked path that had been cleared of junk.
Suddenly, you noticed that the nose of the transporter constantly pulled off to one side and you had to crank the wheel to get it back on the road. And the farther you went, the harder you had to work the wheel.
At last, you stopped and looked about. Your fears were entirely confirmed. There was a moveable crane on the ceiling from which was suspended an enormous industrial magnet that had attracted a pile of small pieces of iron. That's why you hadn't noticed it right away. And now the transporter you were riding on was threatened with the same fate as the pieces of iron.
Something must be done quickly.
loc.56.0: You nearly got stuck behind some huge amorphous piece of plastic, but even so you did manage to break through to the adjacent path, which turned out to be even narrower than the one you had been driving on. However, the magnetic attraction was hardly noticeable here, so you were able to reach the end of the hall without trouble.
loc.56.1:
You climbed out of the transporter's cabin, took aim, adjusted for the lack of wind, half-closed one eye, and lobbed a grenade with precision into the cabin. It fell into an open window and tumbled inside. You immediately dove backwards from the T-3400 and grabbed whatever you could with your hands. An explosion thundered and the magnetic attraction instantly dropped to zero.
Together with a heap of garbage, you fell down with a deafening crash. You were lucky in that the transporter didn't hit the roof. You gave yourself a lump on the forehead, while the transporter itself sustained a bit of damage. However, it remained operational and generally speaking you could keep going. And that's just what you did - as soon as you extracted yourself from a heap of scrap metal.
loc.56.2:
You duly fired up the engine and flew forward, praying that you wouldn't be pulled in by the magnet. Fortunately, you were going fast enough and you rushed by, though the transporter did make a giant leap into the air in the process. But as soon as you touched down, you met an enormous chunk of plating that you had punched through the nose of the T-3400. Despite the deep scratches on the hull that resulted from this acrobatic maneuver, you managed to overcome the obstacle. 
The magnetic attraction grew weaker and weaker until it disappeared entirely at the end of the hall. You can move forward in peace.
loc.57.0:
You decided to put the pedal to the metal and ripped forward, desperately maneuvering to avoid flying into one of the heaps of garbage. Unfortunately, your efforts were in vain, because as you passed under the magnet itself the transporter shot upward and became fixed to the rest of the garbage at a height of ten meters. You seem to be stuck for good.
You probably just need to somehow turn off the magnet so your transporter will be released.
loc.57.1: You took a couple of shots in the direction of the crane cabin, but the control panel inside proved to be well protected and your efforts accomplished nothing. You'll have to think of something else, otherwise somewhere far from here the majority of the pirates will probably be slaughtered.
loc.57.2:
You threw a smoke grenade upward and then wondered what in the world you hoped to accomplish by doing this. It would be unlikely to cause an explosion big enough to shut down the control panel in the crane cabin. 
Fortunately, you didn't have to wonder long, because you missed the mark altogether. The grenade hit the bottom of the cabin, bounced off, fell onto the road, and began to smoke, symbolizing the complete failure of your idea.
loc.59.0:
You wet your hands with spit, climbed out of the transporter and began to scramble up the garbage clinging to the magnet. After reaching the top, you began climbing the line. This wasn't very difficult, because it was thick and covered in sharp burrs from split strands. Ignoring the fact that you got all scratched up and turned red from the rust, the ascent wasn't bad at all.
You climbed into the crane cabin and found everything covered in a thick layer of dust. Apparently, for some reason the crane had not been used for a long time. You instantly understood why when you pulled down the switch supplying the voltage and suffered a severe electrical shock. Unfortunately, your body couldn't endure such a jolt and were left in the crane cabin to live as a ghost.
loc.60.0: You followed the readings on the radar which indicated that to one side of your road there was another small corridor located farther from the magnet. You might be able to use it to cross the hall unimpeded.
loc.61.0: You reached a small platform that ends in a sharp drop. Instinct tells you that your path has nearly come to an end, but you must first get to the other side. There is a retractable bridge that connects your platform with the next, but it's partially pulled away from the other side - and the control panel isn't in sight. Fortunately, you remembered that automatic bridges like this are equipped with emergency switches that operate on a broad spectrum. This knowledge may come in handy.
loc.62.0: You shrugged your shoulders, deciding it couldn't hurt to give it a try. Then you turned on a light and pointed it at the retractable bridge. At first, nothing happened and you sighed in disappointment. But then the track jittered and moved toward your platform. You let out a cry of joy and drove onto the bridge as soon as it was fully extended. Then you carefully moved to the next platform, got out, looked around, and realized that you had arrived. The only thing ahead is the docking hangar, to which the military base is moored. Well, you stayed with the pirates for a while. Now it's time to call on the unwelcome invaders.
loc.62.1:
You set the Jumpmeter's charge level, slammed the gas pedal, and the transporter shot forward. You waited until it was on the very edge of the abyss and pressed the large - but for some reason, not red - button. The T-3400 flew through the air like some giant had kicked it, while you went still, sprawled out in the driver's seat.

Overall, things went very smoothly. The transporter flew as far as could be expected, landed with precision on the bridge, leapt into the air once again and came to a stop in the very center of the platform. You convulsed off of the seat and carefully put your jaw back into place, which you had dislocated from screaming. Then you got out, looked around, and realized that you had arrived. The only thing ahead is the docking hangar, to which the military base is moored. Well, you stayed with the pirates for a while. Now it's time to call on the unwelcome invaders.
loc.63.0:
You surveyed the situation. The size of the platform was approximately <clr>8<clrEnd> meters by <clr>10<clrEnd> meters. After brainstorming with yourself a bit, you determined that if you drove the T-3400 up to the edge of the precipice, then the small lip along the platform edge would help you reach the bridge. This requires the charge level of the Jumpmeter installed on your transporter to be between <clr>10 - 12<clrEnd> units, otherwise you will either fly into the bridge or not reach it at all. Rocking back and forth slightly on the platform, you determined that one second of motion would charge the kinetisizer <clr>1<clrEnd> unit and that turning the gravicar around would drain the charge <clr>2<clrEnd> units. This information could very well help you charge your Jumpmeter to the required level.
You turned the gravicar away from the precipice. Now it's time to start your maneuvers.
loc.63.1: As the transporter's motor purred, you were filled with determination and even began to whistle a lively tune.
loc.65.0:
You set the Jumpmeter's charge level, slammed the gas pedal, and the transporter shot forward. You waited until it was on the very edge of the abyss and pressed the large - but for some reason, not red - button. The T-3400 flew through the air like some giant had kicked it, while you went still, sprawled out in the driver's seat.

Unfortunately, the charge level wasn't high enough. The nose of your transporter barely clipped the retractable bridge. Then it fell into the abyss, dropping lower and lower until it smashed into the bottom.
loc.65.1:
You set the Jumpmeter's charge level, slammed the gas pedal, and the transporter shot forward. You waited until it was on the very edge of the abyss and pressed the large - but for some reason, not red - button. The T-3400 flew through the air like some giant had kicked it, while you went still, sprawled out in the driver's seat.

Unfortunately, the charge level was too high. The transporter flew into the bridge, rammed its nose onto the platform, slid to the side, and before you could say a word the wrecked car rolled over the edge of the platform and fell into the abyss, falling lower and lower until it smashed into the bottom.
loc.67.0: Just as you expected, the guard post wasn't left unattended. So you had to drive up while large-caliber cannon fire came down on your transporter. Most inopportunely, you forgot that you weren't riding in a tank. Several of the shots pierced the hull and hit the engine and fuel tank. Your T-3400 shuttered and disappeared in the flash of a dazzling explosion.
loc.68.0: You approached some gates identical to those from which you took the T-3400, except these gates were labeled: "Sorting Room". They similarly opened automatically, letting you pass.
loc.68.1:
You approached some gates identical to those from which you took the T-3400, except these gates were labeled: "Sorting Room". They similarly opened automatically, letting you pass.
The light on the control panel began to blink treacherously. Apparently, the fuel was gone and something had to be done quickly.
loc.68.2: Finally, you walked up to still more gates. These gates were suspiciously reminiscent of the gates that opened only when you approached them in the T-3400. Without special clothing you came right up next to the gates, but it turns out they didn't want to let you pass. You'll have to go back.
loc.68.3: Finally, you walked up to still more gates. These gates were suspiciously reminiscent of the gates that opened only when you approached them in the T-3400.  Your transporter is still here, standing by the open gates and patiently waiting for your return.
loc.68.4: You donned your thinking cap and realized that first of all you need to get hold of some fuel, because the transporter won't go without it. So you climbed out, grabbed a fuel can from the cargo compartment, and set off to find somebody who would give you some flammable liquid.
loc.68.5: In the body, you found a funnel, stuck it into the fuel hole, and poured fuel from the can. Now you have something to run on, but not for very long. After all, the fuel tank is big and the transporter eats as much fuel as anyone could want. Refueling clearly won't bother you.
loc.69.0: You are in a spacious room. One of its walls is lined with a row of fueling machines. Looks like you could come by some fuel for you T-3400 here.
loc.69.1: You drove up to one of the fueling machines and hopped out of the transporter. After searching for the door to the fuel tank, you found it at the rear near the engine. Then you took the hose from the fueling apparatus and begin pouring fuel into the tank.
loc.69.2: You walked up to the closest fueling machine, pulled out the hose, and quickly filled a full fuel can. Now you can return to the transporter. You just hoped that your spine wouldn't split in two on the way due to the weight of the fuel.
